newsitem.title: USA: NYNEX worldwide access lines grow 4.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: NYNEX worldwide access lines grow 4.7 pct.

text.p: NYNEX Corp said access line demand grew at a record pace -- 4.7 percent worldwide and 3.5 percent in the Northeast, while cellular operations grew by 31.4 percent over 1995.
It said Bell Atlantic NYNEX Mobile (BANM) added more than one million customers in 1996 and ended the year with more than 4.4 million. BANM revenues grew by 29.2 percent in 1996.

At NYNEX's overseas operations in the U.K., Thailand and the Philippines, access lines grew by more than 62 percent, while cellular partnerships in Greece and Indonesia nearly doubled the number of customers.
Earlier, NYNEX reported increases in fourth quarter and year-end earnings on stronger sales.

Telecommunications revenue grew by 3.1 percent over 1995 on strong sales of business and value-added services and increasing network use, NYNEX said. Private line revenues grew 11.3 percent for the year, its 10th consecutive quarterly increase in one of its most competitive market segments. Value-added service revenues were up 31.2 percent over 1995.
Total access minutes of use grew 10.2 percent, and NYNEX said it sold more than 2.5 million new calling plans in New York and Massachusetts.

The company said cable television subscriber growth at NYNEX CableComms was up more than 36 percent over 1995, as new marketing programs increased the number of customers to 268,500 and drove penetration above 20 percent for the first time.

"NYNEX had another outstanding year, with our second consecutive double-digit increase in earnings per share -- a first in our corporation's 12-year history," said NYNEX chairman and chief executive Ivan Seidenberg.

"1996 was an historic year for our progress and our growth. The framework of the local exchange business was changed forever by the Telecommunications Act, which opened long distance and cable television markets to us as well. To take full advantage of these opportunities, we announced one of the largest mergers in U.S. history.

"Throughout these extraordinary changes, we drove top-line growth, met our goals for productivity improvement and sustained our double-digit performance of the previous year. At the same time, by taking aggressive actions, we finished 1996 with significantly improved service results and positioned ourselves to resume the marketing of value-added services and accelerate revenue growth per access line," Seidenberg said.
